definitions.explanation: Describes something that is exactly the right amount, size, timing, or degree — neither too much nor too little.

examples.japanese: このサイズはちょうどいい。
ちょうどいいタイミングで{電話|でんわ}が{来|き}た。
examples.english: A phone call came at just the right time.

examples.japanese: {味|あじ}つけがちょうどいいので、{何|なに}も{足|た}さなくていい。
examples.english: The seasoning is just right, so you don't need to add anything.

notes:
A very common colloquial expression combining ちょうど (exactly) with いい (good). Used constantly in everyday conversation to describe things that fit perfectly — temperature, timing, amount, size, distance, etc.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ちょうどいい{大|おお}きさ: just the right size
- ちょうどいい{量|りょう}: just the right amount
- ちょうどいいタイミング: perfect timing
- ちょうどいい{距離|きょり}: just the right distance
- ちょうどいい{温度|おんど}: just the right temperature

USAGE:
Can be used as a predicate (ちょうどいい) or as a modifier before nouns (ちょうどいい + noun). Unlike many い-adjectives, this is a fixed phrase and does not conjugate as a single unit — the いい part conjugates normally: ちょうどよかった (was just right), ちょうどよくない (not quite right).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ぴったり: fits perfectly (emphasizes exact fit, often physical)
- {適切|てきせつ}: appropriate (more formal, used in writing)
